title: Single-Threaded CPU
summary: Given a 2D integer array of tasks, where each task is represented by [enqueueTime, processingTime], determine the order in which a single-threaded CPU will process these tasks.
statement: Given a 2D integer array of tasks, where each task is represented by [enqueueTime, processingTime], determine the order in which a single-threaded CPU will process these tasks. The CPU will select the task with the shortest processing time; if there are multiple tasks with the same shortest processing time, it will choose the one with the smallest index. The CPU processes tasks continuously until a new task becomes available.
constraints: Each task is [enqueue_time,processing_time] and the CPU runs one task to completion.
Among available tasks choose shortest processing time, breaking ties by original index; return processing order.
hints: Sort tasks by arrival and keep currently available work in a priority queue.
The heap key is processing time followed by original index.
When empty, jump time to the next arrival; enqueue all tasks now available, pop one, and advance time.
The heap exactly represents eligible tasks at every decision, so choosing its minimum follows both scheduling rules without preemption.
editorial: The heap exactly represents eligible tasks at every decision, so choosing its minimum follows both scheduling rules without preemption.

tests.explanation: Task zero runs first; then priorities select tasks two, three, and one.
All arrive together, so duration and then index order gives [4,3,2,0,1].
